Fix my skill's triggering and polish its discovery surfaces.

2. Map descriptions, commands, references, and handoff contracts.
3. Audit for: description mismatches, overlapping triggers, stale names/counts, broken handoffs, missing reference files.
4. Make minimal evidenced edits to fix each finding.

3. Output: audit findings + rewrite options side-by-side.

```
The Tune-Skill skill just fixed this skill's internal triggering and boundaries.
Now audit its external discoverability surfaces and generate polished alternatives.

Focus on:
- GitHub About text and topics that match the tuned description
- README opening line that reflects the new scope and boundaries
- Site page entry that aligns with sibling skills (no overlap)

[Path to the skill's repo or site page]

Chain two existing skills into a single workflow: **Keyword-Guard** audits keyword cannibalization and assigns query ownership, then **Wordsmith** generates alternative titles, H1s, meta descriptions, and content adjustments that resolve internal competition while preserving search intent.

## Invocation

```text
/keyword-resolver [paste target keywords + current pages]
/keyword-resolver https://example.com/sitemap.xml
Resolve cannibalization for "agent skill" and "SEO audit".

- A sitemap URL to inventory
- Search Console data (page + query export)

### Phase 1: Run Keyword-Guard Audit

Invoke the **Keyword-Guard skill** with the provided inputs:

1. If GSC access: query dimensions `page + query` for each target keyword, list every page ranking.
2. If no GSC: pull sitemap, inventory URLs by title/H1/body mentions, flag homepage vs sub-page conflicts.
3. Assign ownership: one query → one owner (most clicks/impressions, closest semantic match).

For each cannibalization conflict identified below, generate 2–3 alternative versions

- H1 headings: de-optimize non-owners, keep owners aligned
- Meta descriptions: clarify unique value per page
- Content adjustments: strip competing primary keywords from non-owners
- Hreflang fixes: declare full reciprocal sets for multi-language pages

Original audit:
[Paste keyword-guard's full report here]

Target pages:
[List the specific URLs flagged for each conflict]
```

- Treat each conflict as a separate rewrite task
- Provide 2–3 options per page (labeled Option A/B/C)
- Keep the author's voice and facts intact
- Highlight which option best resolves each cannibalization issue

1. **Keyword-Guard Ownership Map** (one query → one owner, conflicts listed)

User: /keyword-resolver "agent skill" and "SEO audit"

# keyword-resolver

- Two pages rank for the same keyword and neither ranks well
- Search Console shows multiple pages getting impressions for one query
- You have mixed-language pages competing with each other
- Someone asks "which page should rank for X?"
- You want to build a keyword cluster map for your site

# Tune skill

Fine-tuning is a set of small, evidenced edits to a skill that already exists. It is not a rewrite. The goal is a skill that triggers on the right requests, stays out of its siblings' way, and passes work along in a defined shape.

## Ground rules

- **Read the real SKILL.md first.** READMEs, repo descriptions and listings drift from the file the agent actually loads. Any claim about a skill must come from its SKILL.md or its references. If you can't open a file, name it and say what you are inferring instead.
- **Check your own claims.** If a file you read later contradicts something you said earlier, say so plainly and correct it. Don't quietly route around it.
- **Minimal edits, the author's voice.** Change what the audit found and nothing else. Keep frontmatter keys you don't recognise (`version`, `argument-hint`, `user-invocable`). Never weaken honesty, safety or privacy rules.
- **Don't claim what you didn't run.** Say which checks ran, which test cases were only written, and which files you never saw.

## Workflow

### 1. Collect

Get the SKILL.md of the target skill and of every sibling it touches, plus any references you can reach. If the user gives a link you can't open, ask for the file text or its URL. If the skill is a folder on disk, run the check script (step 6) now for a first read.

### 2. Map

Write a short inventory per skill: what its description promises, its modes or commands, the reference files it names, and what it hands off and to whom. Put sibling descriptions and command lists side by side. Overlaps only show up when you can see both.

### 3. Audit

Work through `references/audit-checklist.md`. For each finding record the evidence (quote the line), the severity (breaks triggering, confusing, or cosmetic) and the smallest fix. Report the most severe first.

### 4. Settle boundaries

When two skills claim the same request, give it one owner. Use the split the user's own design already uses (for example verdict versus artifact: one skill judges, the other writes). Ask the user only when their design doesn't settle it, and ask once.

### 5. Edit

Make the smallest change that fixes each finding. When the user will drop the result straight into a repo, hand back whole replacement files and copy untouched text exactly. When a fix needs a new shared piece (a handoff format, say), add a new reference file instead of editing one you haven't seen. List any reference files that probably need a matching update.

### 6. Validate

Run the check script on each skill folder:

```
python scripts/check_skill.py <path-to-skill-folder>
```

It checks that the name matches the folder, the description fits the 1024-character limit and has trigger and boundary wording, the H1 matches the name, referenced files exist, and the body stays a reasonable length. Fix every FAIL. Judge each WARN. A NOTE means the body ties the skill to a moment Claude does not choose (before pushing, deploying, releasing); see section H of the checklist. The script reads CRLF and BOM files and works without PyYAML; `python -I scripts/test_check_skill.py` is its self-check. If you only have pasted text, save the SKILL.md into a folder named after the skill and run it there; missing-reference warnings are expected in that case.

### 7. Write test cases

Follow `references/test-cases.md`. Every boundary you changed gets one case on each side. Run them by hand against the descriptions. Some agents ship an automated triggering loop in their authoring tooling; if you didn't run one, don't imply you did. Say which you did.

### 8. Regress the family

One skill's fix can break a sibling: a reworded description now shares a trigger phrase, or a
renamed skill leaves "(use old-name)" behind elsewhere. After editing, re-check every skill in the
family against the last accepted state:

```
python scripts/regress.py <folder-of-skills> [more folders] --baseline health.json
python scripts/regress.py <folders> --baseline health.json --write   # accept, once reviewed
```

It runs `check_skill.py` on every SKILL.md it finds and adds two family-wide checks: a dangling
handoff (a description says "(use X)" and no X is in the family) and a trigger collision (two
descriptions quote the same phrase). Anything new since the baseline is a regression and exits 1;
anything that went away is an improvement. Pass skills that live elsewhere with
`--external name,name`. Write the baseline only after reading the regressions, never to silence
them. Keep `health.json` next to the family (a site repo, a marketplace) so a scheduled CI job can
run the same command and open an issue when it fails; `python -I scripts/test_regress.py` is its
self-check.

### 9. Report

Keep it short:

- What changed, per skill, and why (one line each).
- Corrections to anything you said earlier.
- What you could not see or did not run.
# The GitHub listing

Contents: [About text](#about-text) · [Topics](#topics) · [Homepage](#homepage) · [README opening](#readme-opening) · [Release notes](#release-notes) · [Social preview](#social-preview) · [License](#license) · [Kit format](#kit-format) · [Apply commands](#apply-commands) · [Project-type notes](#project-type-notes)

## About text

The About description is shown in search results and on directory cards, so it has to make sense with no other context.

- Limit: 350 characters. Aim for 200 to 280.
- Formula: what it is, for what task, with the guarantee or differentiator, and where it works. For example: "Agent skill that reviews resumes the way recruiters screen them: ATS check, rejection reasons, gap analysis. Never invents metrics. Works with Claude Code, Cursor and Qoder."
- Start with the category and task, matching the target queries. Do not open with the project name; it already appears next to the text.
- Plain words. No emoji, no superlatives, no claims the repo cannot back.

## Topics

Topics feed GitHub's topic pages and search.

- At most 20. Each is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 50 characters. Use 10 to 15.
- Mix three kinds: type (`agent-skills`, `claude-code`, `mcp-server`), domain (`resume`, `ats`, `seo`), and platform (`cursor`, `qoder`).
- Prefer topics that already have a page with other projects on it; an unused topic helps nobody find you. Check `github.com/topics/<name>`.
- Only true topics. Do not add a popular topic the project does not belong to.
- Skip generic filler (`ai`, `tool`, `app`) unless it really is the core category.

## Homepage

Set it to the project's page on the user's own site if one exists, otherwise leave it empty. The About panel then links the repo and the site to each other.

## README opening

The first screen decides whether a visitor stays and what a search snippet shows.

1. `# project-name`
2. **A first paragraph** that names the task, audience and guarantee in plain words, using the target-query phrases: "A resume and LinkedIn review agent skill for Claude Code, Cursor and Qoder. It checks your resume the way a recruiter screens it..."
3. **One install line**, owner-qualified, e.g. `npx skills add owner/repo --skill name`.
4. **"Ask it things like"** with three or four prompts a user would type.
5. **A disambiguation line** if any same-name project exists: what this is, what the other one is, and that they are unrelated.
6. **A sibling line** if there are related projects, saying who does what.

Keep this above the first heading below the fold. Do not add badges before the first paragraph.

## Release notes

Cut a first tagged release (`v0.1.0`). Notes are factual: what it does, the commands or tools included, and the install command. A repo with no releases looks unfinished, and some listings read releases.

## Social preview

An image shown when the repo link is shared. Describe what it should contain for the user to produce: the project name, the one-line pitch, and the install line, large and legible. GitHub's current recommendation is a 1280 by 640 pixel image under 1 MB; confirm in the repo's Settings before relying on those numbers.

## License

Check for a `LICENSE` file. If missing, tell the user and ask which license they want; do not pick one for them.

## Kit format

Write About and Topics in exactly this shape in `discovery-kit.md`, so `scripts/check_listing.py --kit discovery-kit.md` can find them:

````
**About (description, 350 character limit):**

```

- **Read the real SKILL.md first.** READMEs, repo descriptions and listings drift from the file the agent actually loads. Any claim about a skill must come from its SKILL.md or its references. If you can't open a file, name it and say what you are inferring instead.
- **Check your own claims.** If a file you read later contradicts something you said earlier, say so plainly and correct it. Don't quietly route around it.
- **Minimal edits, the author's voice.** Change what the audit found and nothing else. Keep frontmatter keys you don't recognise (`version`, `argument-hint`, `user-invocable`). Never weaken honesty, safety or privacy rules.
- **Don't claim what you didn't run.** Say which checks ran, which test cases were only written, and which files you never saw.

## Workflow

### 1. Collect

Get the SKILL.md of the target skill and of every sibling it touches, plus any references you can reach. If the user gives a link you can't open, ask for the file text or its URL. If the skill is a folder on disk, run the check script (step 6) now for a first read.

### 2. Map

Write a short inventory per skill: what its description promises, its modes or commands, the reference files it names, and what it hands off and to whom. Put sibling descriptions and command lists side by side. Overlaps only show up when you can see both.

### 3. Audit

Work through `references/audit-checklist.md`. For each finding record the evidence (quote the line), the severity (breaks triggering, confusing, or cosmetic) and the smallest fix. Report the most severe first.

### 4. Settle boundaries

When two skills claim the same request, give it one owner. Use the split the user's own design already uses (for example verdict versus artifact: one skill judges, the other writes). Ask the user only when their design doesn't settle it, and ask once.

### 5. Edit

Make the smallest change that fixes each finding. When the user will drop the result straight into a repo, hand back whole replacement files and copy untouched text exactly. When a fix needs a new shared piece (a handoff format, say), add a new reference file instead of editing one you haven't seen. List any reference files that probably need a matching update.

### 6. Validate

Run the check script on each skill folder:

```
python scripts/check_skill.py <path-to-skill-folder>
```

It checks that the name matches the folder, the description fits the 1024-character limit and has trigger and boundary wording, the H1 matches the name, referenced files exist, and the body stays a reasonable length. Fix every FAIL. Judge each WARN. A NOTE means the body ties the skill to a moment Claude does not choose (before pushing, deploying, releasing); see section H of the checklist. The script reads CRLF and BOM files and works without PyYAML; `python -I scripts/test_check_skill.py` is its self-check. If you only have pasted text, save the SKILL.md into a folder named after the skill and run it there; missing-reference warnings are expected in that case.

### 7. Write test cases

Follow `references/test-cases.md`. Every boundary you changed gets one case on each side. Run them by hand against the descriptions. Some agents ship an automated triggering loop in their authoring tooling; if you didn't run one, don't imply you did. Say which you did.

### 8. Regress the family

One skill's fix can break a sibling: a reworded description now shares a trigger phrase, or a
renamed skill leaves "(use old-name)" behind elsewhere. After editing, re-check every skill in the
family against the last accepted state:

```
python scripts/regress.py <folder-of-skills> [more folders] --baseline health.json
python scripts/regress.py <folders> --baseline health.json --write   # accept, once reviewed
```

It runs `check_skill.py` on every SKILL.md it finds and adds two family-wide checks: a dangling
handoff (a description says "(use X)" and no X is in the family) and a trigger collision (two
descriptions quote the same phrase). Anything new since the baseline is a regression and exits 1;
anything that went away is an improvement. Pass skills that live elsewhere with
`--external name,name`. Write the baseline only after reading the regressions, never to silence
them. Keep `health.json` next to the family (a site repo, a marketplace) so a scheduled CI job can
run the same command and open an issue when it fails; `python -I scripts/test_regress.py` is its
self-check.

### 9. Report

Keep it short:

- What changed, per skill, and why (one line each).
- Corrections to anything you said earlier.
- What you could not see or did not run.

# Keyword-Resolver

Chain two existing skills into a single workflow: **Keyword-Guard** audits keyword cannibalization and assigns query ownership, then **Wordsmith** generates alternative titles, H1s, meta descriptions, and content adjustments that resolve internal competition while preserving search intent.

## Invocation

```text
/keyword-resolver [paste target keywords + current pages]
/keyword-resolver https://example.com/sitemap.xml
Resolve cannibalization for "agent skill" and "SEO audit".
```

If no target is provided, ask the user for either:
- A list of target keywords + the pages currently ranking for them
- A sitemap URL to inventory
- Search Console data (page + query export)

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Run Keyword-Guard Audit

Invoke the **Keyword-Guard skill** with the provided inputs:

1. If GSC access: query dimensions `page + query` for each target keyword, list every page ranking.
2. If no GSC: pull sitemap, inventory URLs by title/H1/body mentions, flag homepage vs sub-page conflicts.
3. Assign ownership: one query → one owner (most clicks/impressions, closest semantic match).
4. Identify cannibalization: pages sharing primary keyword in title+H1, mixed-language conflicts without hreflang.
5. Output: a structured ownership map with conflict findings and resolution plan.

**Handoff rule:** Capture keyword-guard's full audit output verbatim. Do not summarize yet.

### Phase 2: Generate Alternatives with Wordsmith

Pass keyword-guard's audit findings to the **Wordsmith skill** with this instruction:

```
For each cannibalization conflict identified below, generate 2–3 alternative versions
that resolve the competition while preserving search intent. Focus on:

- Title tags: rewrite non-owners to distinct long-tail modifiers
- H1 headings: de-optimize non-owners, keep owners aligned
- Meta descriptions: clarify unique value per page
- Content adjustments: strip competing primary keywords from non-owners
- Hreflang fixes: declare full reciprocal sets for multi-language pages

Original audit:
[Paste keyword-guard's full report here]

Target pages:
[List the specific URLs flagged for each conflict]
```

Wordsmith should:
- Treat each conflict as a separate rewrite task
- Provide 2–3 options per page (labeled Option A/B/C)
- Keep the author's voice and facts intact
- Highlight which option best resolves each cannibalization issue

### Phase 3: Present Results

Return a three-part response:

1. **Keyword-Guard Ownership Map** (one query → one owner, conflicts listed)
2. **Wordsmith Alternatives** (grouped by conflict, with options labeled per page)
3. **Recommended Actions** (which combination of alternatives to apply, plus internal linking changes, in 2–3 sentences)

Format the alternatives so the user can copy-paste directly into their CMS or HTML files.

## Example

```
User: /keyword-resolver "agent skill" and "SEO audit"

Assistant:

## Keyword-Guard Ownership Map

**Query: "agent skill"**
- Owner: /skills/findable-polish (12 clicks, 45 impressions)
- Competing: /skills/findable (8 clicks, 30 impressions), / (homepage, 5 clicks, 20 impressions)
- Conflict: All three share "agent skill" in title+H1

**Query: "SEO audit"**
- Owner: /skills/seo-audit (20 clicks, 60 impressions)
- Competing: /skills/keyword-guard (3 clicks, 10 impressions)
- Conflict: keyword-guard's title mentions "SEO audit" but it's not the owner

## Wordsmith Alternatives

### Conflict 1: "agent skill" — /skills/findable

**Option A:** Title: "Repo Discovery Audit for AI Agents" | H1: "Make Your Repos Findable by Agents"
**Option B:** Title: "GitHub Visibility Audit for Skills" | H1: "Audit Repo Discoverability Gaps"
**Option C:** Title: "Agent Skill Discovery Setup" | H1: "Set Up GitHub Discovery for Agent Skills"

→ Best: Option A (removes "agent skill" from title, keeps semantic relevance)

[... continues for each conflict ...]

## Recommended Actions

1. Apply Option A to /skills/findable title+H1.
2. Add internal link FROM /skills/findable TO /skills/findable-polish with anchor "workflow that polishes discoverability".
3. Rewrite /skills/keyword-guard title to "SEO Keyword Cluster Planner" to stop competing with seo-audit.
4. Declare hreflang set for /ar/skills/* if Arabic locale exists (currently missing return tags).
```

## Boundaries

- **Does not** execute technical crawl/index/perf diagnosis (use seo-audit for that).
- **Does not** generate mass template pages (use programmatic-seo for that).
- **Does not** change canonical tags across locales unless explicitly asked (cross-canonical suppresses indexing).
- **Does not** access GSC automatically — works from pasted exports or sitemap inventory.

## Dependencies

This skill requires both `keyword-guard` and `wordsmith` to be installed. If either is missing, tell the user and stop.

# Keyword-Resolver

Chain two existing skills into a single workflow: **Keyword-Guard** audits keyword cannibalization and assigns query ownership, then **Wordsmith** generates alternative titles, H1s, meta descriptions, and content adjustments that resolve internal competition while preserving search intent.

## Invocation

```text
/keyword-resolver [paste target keywords + current pages]
/keyword-resolver https://example.com/sitemap.xml
Resolve cannibalization for "agent skill" and "SEO audit".
```

If no target is provided, ask the user for either:
- A list of target keywords + the pages currently ranking for them
- A sitemap URL to inventory
- Search Console data (page + query export)

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Run Keyword-Guard Audit

Invoke the **Keyword-Guard skill** with the provided inputs:

1. If GSC access: query dimensions `page + query` for each target keyword, list every page ranking.
2. If no GSC: pull sitemap, inventory URLs by title/H1/body mentions, flag homepage vs sub-page conflicts.
3. Assign ownership: one query → one owner (most clicks/impressions, closest semantic match).
4. Identify cannibalization: pages sharing primary keyword in title+H1, mixed-language conflicts without hreflang.
5. Output: a structured ownership map with conflict findings and resolution plan.

**Handoff rule:** Capture keyword-guard's full audit output verbatim. Do not summarize yet.

### Phase 2: Generate Alternatives with Wordsmith

Pass keyword-guard's audit findings to the **Wordsmith skill** with this instruction:

```
For each cannibalization conflict identified below, generate 2–3 alternative versions
that resolve the competition while preserving search intent. Focus on:

- Title tags: rewrite non-owners to distinct long-tail modifiers
- H1 headings: de-optimize non-owners, keep owners aligned
- Meta descriptions: clarify unique value per page
- Content adjustments: strip competing primary keywords from non-owners
- Hreflang fixes: declare full reciprocal sets for multi-language pages

Original audit:
[Paste keyword-guard's full report here]

Target pages:
[List the specific URLs flagged for each conflict]
```

Wordsmith should:
- Treat each conflict as a separate rewrite task
- Provide 2–3 options per page (labeled Option A/B/C)
- Keep the author's voice and facts intact
- Highlight which option best resolves each cannibalization issue

### Phase 3: Present Results

Return a three-part response:

1. **Keyword-Guard Ownership Map** (one query → one owner, conflicts listed)
2. **Wordsmith Alternatives** (grouped by conflict, with options labeled per page)
3. **Recommended Actions** (which combination of alternatives to apply, plus internal linking changes, in 2–3 sentences)

Format the alternatives so the user can copy-paste directly into their CMS or HTML files.

## Example

```
User: /keyword-resolver "agent skill" and "SEO audit"

Assistant:

## Keyword-Guard Ownership Map

**Query: "agent skill"**
- Owner: /skills/findable-polish (12 clicks, 45 impressions)
- Competing: /skills/findable (8 clicks, 30 impressions), / (homepage, 5 clicks, 20 impressions)
- Conflict: All three share "agent skill" in title+H1

**Query: "SEO audit"**
- Owner: /skills/seo-audit (20 clicks, 60 impressions)
- Competing: /skills/keyword-guard (3 clicks, 10 impressions)
- Conflict: keyword-guard's title mentions "SEO audit" but it's not the owner

## Wordsmith Alternatives

### Conflict 1: "agent skill" — /skills/findable

**Option A:** Title: "Repo Discovery Audit for AI Agents" | H1: "Make Your Repos Findable by Agents"
**Option B:** Title: "GitHub Visibility Audit for Skills" | H1: "Audit Repo Discoverability Gaps"
**Option C:** Title: "Agent Skill Discovery Setup" | H1: "Set Up GitHub Discovery for Agent Skills"

→ Best: Option A (removes "agent skill" from title, keeps semantic relevance)

[... continues for each conflict ...]

## Recommended Actions

1. Apply Option A to /skills/findable title+H1.
2. Add internal link FROM /skills/findable TO /skills/findable-polish with anchor "workflow that polishes discoverability".
3. Rewrite /skills/keyword-guard title to "SEO Keyword Cluster Planner" to stop competing with seo-audit.
4. Declare hreflang set for /ar/skills/* if Arabic locale exists (currently missing return tags).
```

- **Does not** change canonical tags across locales unless explicitly asked (cross-canonical suppresses indexing).
